$schema-note: Deterministic asset budgets for issue #33. All limits are RAW bytes (uncompressed file size) measured from the production `astro build` output by web/tests/build/asset-budgets.test.ts. Raw bytes are gated because, for a given source tree, they are identical on any machine -- no compressor, so no zlib/brotli version variance. (Two pages, home and compare, stamp the build date via `new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)`, a fixed-width 10-char field: its byte LENGTH is stable across days even though its content is not, so the budgeted number does not move with the calendar.) gzip and brotli are reported by `npm run assets:report` for realism but never gated. There is no override, skip or force flag; an intentional exception is an explicit entry here with a stated reason, which is reviewable, never a bypass.
headroom-note: Ceilings sit ~12-26% above the value measured when they were set, leaving room for normal catalog growth while still reddening on a real regression -- and because a raw-byte budget is a claim about the whole built tree, it goes stale on any markup or data change by anyone, which no file-collision check can detect. The measured baseline for each entry is recorded in `measuredRaw` so the headroom is auditable. The ceilings were raised (home, catalog, updates, providers) for three causes measured earlier: the BASE_PATH=/ModelTree/ pin (+380..+5449 per route, the deploy prefix CI applies that a local root build did not), #634's SEO head markup (canonical, robots, 9 Open Graph + 5 Twitter tags, small inline JSON-LD, on every route), and #647's variant-positioning dataset plus expanded LineageExplorer/ModelPassport inlining more per-model tier data. Re-baselined on 2026-08-31 against trunk 7c506bd1 (the current rebased merge-base). Two prior re-baselines are folded into the measured values: #665 (long-tail family depth, +728..+7790 HTML) and then the 7-commit span 356989e9..7c506bd1, whose only structural mover is #674 (render EVERY cited source for a variant-positioning record, not just the first): #674 added ~16 lines to global.css (+117 raw CSS on every route, since the stylesheet is shared) and multi-source HTML to the lineage/variant routes (home +1472, tree/compare +617 each; providers +280 incl. a +165 shared-JS re-chunk from LineageExplorer.tsx). #675 nudged providers/[slug].astro (+4 lines, net ~0). The five data/test-only commits (#668/#671/#673/#676/#680) net near-zero rendered bytes. Every one of these was absorbed within existing headroom, so NO ceiling changed on this re-baseline and each `reason` records where the growth landed.

globals.reason: Whole-build ceilings across _astro/. jsTotal/cssTotal catch shared-bundle and shared-stylesheet growth that no single route surfaces. fontTotal is held tight (+12%) so a new font weight or subset is caught. astroDir is the backstop on total hashed-asset weight. Ceilings sized for #647 (js 424190 -> 435805 component code +11.6k; css 101814 -> 103272 global.css +1.5k; dir 713040 -> 726113), each absorbed by headroom. #665 was a pure data/HTML change that added no _astro weight. On the 7c506bd1 re-baseline #674 (render every cited source) added the first _astro movement since: js 435805 -> 435970 (+165, LineageExplorer.tsx/ModelPassport.tsx re-chunk), css 103272 -> 103389 (+117, its ~16 global.css lines), dir 726113 -> 726395 (+282); font unchanged at 187036. Each absorbed by headroom, no ceiling raised. jsTotal deliberately stays 520000 so it doubles as the NODE_ENV backstop: a dev-React build measures ~670510 raw JS and trips it regardless of the marker assertion. A classifier drift that zeroed a kind is caught by the separate per-kind non-emptiness floor in the test, not by these ceilings.

excludedFromRouteTotals.reason: Issue #34 adds a single static Open Graph card referenced only by an `og:image` tag. Social scrapers fetch it; a visitor on a route never does. The accounting only sums a route's render/hydration resources (stylesheets, island JS,

Generated catalog index endpoint referenced by no route's HTML, so it is never part of a visitor's per-route transfer. Kept out of route totals; whether it has a live consumer is tracked as a follow-up, not decided here.
